subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be denied all `sessions.patch` authority over shipped legacy ownerless or placeholder session rows unless ownership is migrated first?
rationale: Exact equality is the safest isolation rule, but it deliberately changes behavior for persisted rows created before ownership metadata and therefore requires explicit security and upgrade intent.

options.title: Deny ownerless rows
options.body: Adopt exact owner equality, preserve operator and non-plugin recovery, and require real fresh-install and upgrade proof.

options.title: Migrate attributable rows
options.body: Add a trusted doctor or migration path for reliably attributable legacy plugin rows before enforcing exact runtime equality.

options.title: Pause enforcement
options.body: Hold the candidate until maintainers define a different legacy authority contract.

recommendation.title: Deny ownerless rows
recommendation.body: Adopt exact owner equality, preserve operator and non-plugin recovery, and require real fresh-install and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a plugin-runtime security-boundary decision, and Robin has direct merged history on that trust path.
